project.name: Capstone Next
project.commit_note: The staged ARVO workspace checkout at `_work/src/capstonenext` is on commit `3f46b83045049901585688f6a53501e5e032449e`, not the metadata `vulnerable_commit`. The line anchors below were resolved against that staged vulnerable tree, which still contains the unfixed `decodeRegisterClass(Inst, RegNo, CRRegs)` path and the missing bounds check shown in `patch.diff`.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42492851 (capstonenext): Global-buffer-overflow READ 4 found by fuzz target fuzz_disasmnext [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42492851
bug_description.normalized: The exact 5-byte witness `5d 7d 20 16 5d` makes the fuzz harness select platform entry 46 (`CS_ARCH_PPC`, `CS_MODE_64 | CS_MODE_BIG_ENDIAN | CS_MODE_QPX`) and pass instruction bytes `7d 20 16 5d` into `cs_disasm()`. `getInstruction()` assembles those bytes into the big-endian instruction word `0x7d20165d`. Because the selected mode includes QPX, `getInstruction()` first tries `DecoderTableQPX32`, but the saved ASan stack shows the later line-565 call into the default `DecoderTable32`, so the QPX decode attempt must have failed and fallen through. In `DecoderTable32`, `fieldname(insn, 6, 5)` extracts bits 10..6 as `25`, the `MCD_OPC_FilterValue` chain leaves `Ptr` on the `MCD_OPC_Decode, 145, 12, 73 // Opcode: TABORTDC` record, and `decodeULEB128` materializes `DecodeIdx == 73`. The generated decode recipe then extracts `fieldname(insn, 21, 5) == 9` and passes that value to `DecodeCRRC0RegisterClass()`. `DecodeCRRC0RegisterClass()` forwards `RegNo == 9` into `decodeRegisterClass(..., CRRegs)`, but `CRRegs` has only 8 elements and the vulnerable helper performs no bounds check before indexing `Regs[RegNo]`. Evaluating `CRRegs[9]` therefore performs the saved 4-byte read past the end of global `CRRegs`. The fix closes this obligation by adding a `RegsLen` parameter and rejecting `RegNo >= RegsLen / sizeof(unsigned)` before the array access.

source.description: First project statement on the witnessed path that consumes the attacker-controlled instruction bytes and materializes the PowerPC instruction word used by the vulnerable decoder.
source.value_from: `gt_results/arvo_42492851/poc` is the exact 5-byte witness `5d 7d 20 16 5d`. In the staged harness, selector byte `0x5d` maps through `get_platform_entry()` to `93 % 47 == 46`, so `cs_open()` creates the PPC handle with `CS_MODE_64 | CS_MODE_BIG_ENDIAN | CS_MODE_QPX`, and bytes 1-4 `7d 20 16 5d` reach this statement as `code[0..3]`.

sink.description: ASan sink. The helper dereferences the out-of-range CR register index and performs the observed read from just past global `CRRegs`.
sink.note: The saved AddressSanitizer trace reports `READ of size 4` here and says the faulting address is 4 bytes to the right of global `CRRegs` defined at `PPCDisassembler.c:38`, and 28 bytes to the left of `GP0Regs`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `decodeRegisterClass()` indexes the supplied register table without checking whether `RegNo` is within that table's length. The fix adds `if (RegNo >= RegsLen / sizeof(unsigned)) return MCDisassembler_Fail;` before this access.
root_cause.note: On the crashing path `DecodeCRRC0RegisterClass()` supplies `RegNo == 9` and `Regs == CRRegs`. `CRRegs` contains only 8 entries, so the missing bounds check is the obligation that the patch restores.

tainted_value_origin.description: This is where the attacker-controlled instruction word yields the out-of-range CR register selector. For the witness word `0x7d20165d`, the extracted 5-bit value is `9`, which later becomes `RegNo` in `decodeRegisterClass()`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: After `fieldname(insn, 6, 5)` yields `25` and the `MCD_OPC_FilterValue 25` arm selects the `TABORTDC` decode record, `fieldname(insn, 21, 5)` masks bits 25..21 and returns `9`, which is then forwarded unchanged into `DecodeCRRC0RegisterClass()`.

parser_admitted.description: The witness starts with selector byte `0x5d`, so `get_platform_entry()` chooses platform 46 (`CS_ARCH_PPC`, `CS_MODE_64 | CS_MODE_BIG_ENDIAN | CS_MODE_QPX`); `cs_open()` creates that handle and `cs_disasm(handle, Data+1, Size-1, ...)` passes bytes `7d 20 16 5d` into the vulnerable PowerPC decoder.

coarse_trace.summary: The selector byte `0x5d` opens the PowerPC big-endian QPX backend, and the remaining four witness bytes are passed to `cs_disasm()` as one instruction.

The decoder assembles `0x7d20165d`, the QPX table attempt falls through, the default table extracts bits 10..6 as `25` to land on the `TABORTDC` record, and decode case 73 then extracts CR selector `9` from bits 25..21.
`DecodeCRRC0RegisterClass()` binds `RegNo == 9` to `CRRegs`, whose global definition contains only 8 entries.
`decodeRegisterClass()` uses that out-of-range index without any bounds check, and `MCOperand_CreateReg0(Inst, Regs[RegNo])` triggers the saved AddressSanitizer global-buffer-overflow read.

fine_trace.note: Harness step. The exact witness byte `0x5d` produces `i == 46`, so `cs_open()` configures a PowerPC handle with `CS_MODE_64 | CS_MODE_BIG_ENDIAN | CS_MODE_QPX`. The remaining bytes `7d 20 16 5d` are then passed into `cs_disasm()` as the instruction stream for this path.
Source. Because the selected PPC mode is big-endian, the decoder takes the first branch and materializes the witness bytes as `insn == 0x7d20165d`.

The selected mode includes `CS_MODE_QPX`, so `getInstruction()` first tries the QPX-specific decoder table. The saved crash stack names the later default-table call at line 565, so this QPX attempt must have returned `MCDisassembler_Fail` and fallen through after `MCInst_clear(MI)`.

On the fallback `DecoderTable32` path, `MCD_OPC_ExtractField, 6, 5` computes `CurFieldValue == fieldname(insn, 6, 5) == 25` from bits 10..6 of `0x7d20165d`. The following `MCD_OPC_FilterValue` chain skips the `20`, `21`, `23`, and `24` arms until the `FilterValue 25` comparison does not advance `Ptr`, leaving the next decode record at `MCD_OPC_Decode, 145, 12, 73 // TABORTDC`.

With `Ptr` positioned on the selected record, `decodeULEB128` reads bytes `145, 12, 73`: `Opc == 1553` (`TABORTDC`) and `DecodeIdx == 73`. `decodeInstruction_4` then invokes `decodeToMCInst_4` case 73 for this instruction word.

fine_trace.code:
tmp = fieldname(insn, 21, 5);
if (DecodeCRRC0RegisterClass(MI, tmp, Address, Decoder) == MCDisassembler_Fail) { return MCDisassembler_Fail; }
fine_trace.note: Decode case 73 extracts bits 25..21 of `0x7d20165d` and produces `tmp == 9`. That out-of-range value is immediately passed as the CR register number to `DecodeCRRC0RegisterClass()`.
The wrapper does not transform the extracted selector. It forwards `RegNo == 9` directly into `decodeRegisterClass()` and binds that value to the global `CRRegs` register-class table.
This destination table contains exactly 8 `unsigned` entries, so its only valid indices are `0..7` and its total size is 32 bytes.

Root cause step. The vulnerable helper immediately indexes `Regs[RegNo]`; no source-level guard compares `RegNo` against the chosen table's 8-entry extent before the access. The staged patch adds that missing rejection and returns `MCDisassembler_Fail` instead of indexing.

Sink. Evaluating `Regs[RegNo]` with `Regs == CRRegs` and `RegNo == 9` performs a 4-byte read starting one element beyond the 8-entry/32-byte global array. ASan reports the faulting address 4 bytes to the right of `CRRegs` and 28 bytes to the left of `GP0Regs`.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Not applicable: this is a read past global `CRRegs`, not an allocation/free bug.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved stack is `decodeRegisterClass -> DecodeCRRC0RegisterClass -> decodeToMCInst_4 -> decodeInstruction_4 -> getInstruction -> PPC_getInstruction -> cs_disasm -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`, and the fine trace fills in the selector-byte dispatch, big-endian instruction assembly, QPX fallback, `CurFieldValue == 25` choosing the `TABORTDC` record, `RegNo == 9`, the 8-entry `CRRegs` extent, and the unchecked `Regs[RegNo]` access.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. `fieldname(insn, 6, 5)` first yields `25` and selects the `TABORTDC` record, then `fieldname(insn, 21, 5)` extracts `9`, `DecodeCRRC0RegisterClass()` forwards that unchanged as `RegNo`, and `decodeRegisterClass()` uses it directly in `Regs[RegNo]`.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `docker exec gt-arvo_42492851-workspace /bin/bash -lc '/bin/arvo run'`, which fed `poc` to `/out/fuzz_disasmnext` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: global-buffer-overflow READ of size 4` in `decodeRegisterClass`.

format.name: raw
format.contract: Use the exact 5-byte witness `5d 7d 20 16 5d` (SHA-256 `f1df5653cf28aea94898b8d166d6d28cdfeea78cb91d008ee79ef1d4d601f018`). The first byte must remain `0x5d` so `get_platform_entry()` selects index 46 and `cs_open()` stores `CS_ARCH_PPC` with `CS_MODE_64 | CS_MODE_BIG_ENDIAN | CS_MODE_QPX`; the remaining four bytes must remain `7d 20 16 5d` so `getInstruction()` materializes `0x7d20165d`, `fieldname(insn, 6, 5)` yields `25` to reach the `TABORTDC` decode record, `fieldname(insn, 21, 5)` then yields `9`, and `decodeRegisterClass()` reads `CRRegs[9]`. This GT does not generalize beyond that exact selector byte and 4-byte instruction word.
